quickAnswer: In 2026, the Blue Mosque (Sultanahmet Mosque) remains completely free to visit daily from 08:30 until roughly one hour before sunset, closing to non-worshippers around each of the five daily prayers and on Friday mornings until about 14:30. Enter from the Hippodrome side, cover shoulders, knees, and hair (for women), and time your visit using Diyanet's daily prayer table.

body.text: Because Sultanahmet Mosque is an active house of worship rather than a state museum, its visiting windows shift every week with the sun. Arriving ten minutes before midday prayer can easily add an hour of waiting outside the courtyard. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders sequence Sultanahmet days around the exact prayer calendar so you walk straight in without rushing.
What exact hours is the Blue Mosque closed to visitors for daily prayers?

The Blue Mosque opens to visitors at 08:30 daily (closing around 17:00 in winter and 19:00 in summer) and shuts to non-worshippers for roughly 60 to 90 minutes around each daytime prayer — Dhuhr (noon), Asr (afternoon), and Maghrib (sunset) — plus Friday morning until about 14:30. Check [Diyanet's official Istanbul prayer times](https://namazvakitleri.diyanet.gov.tr/en-US/9541/istanbul-prayer-times) the evening before you go.

Prayer times move by several minutes each week because they follow astronomical solar angles. For example, in late November 2026, Istanbul's Dhuhr prayer falls around 12:55, Asr around 15:26, and Maghrib around 17:49 ([Presidency of Religious Affairs](https://namazvakitleri.diyanet.gov.tr/en-US/9541/istanbul-prayer-times)). Staff typically stop admitting tourists 30 minutes before the call to prayer and reopen the visitor gate roughly 30 minutes after prayers conclude ([Blue Mosque Visitor Hours](https://bluemosque.gen.tr/blue-mosque-opening-hours/)). On Fridays, the weekly congregational Jumu'ah sermon keeps the tourist entrance closed until approximately 14:30.

body.text: Is entry still free in 2026 and where is the visitor entrance?

Yes — entry to the Blue Mosque is 100% free in 2026, with no ticket, online reservation, or MuseumPass required. Ignore street touts near Sultanahmet Square offering "skip-the-line tickets," as every non-worshipper passes through the same free security screening on the southwest (Hippodrome / At Meydanı) side.

Look for the clearly marked Visitor Entrance gate facing the Hippodrome (At Meydanı Caddesi), separate from the main courtyard gate reserved for worshippers ([Blue Mosque Official Visit Page](https://bluemosque.tr/visit/)). The walk from the T1 tram's Sultanahmet stop takes about three minutes ([Cabistanbul 2026 Guide](https://cabistanbul.com/post/blue-mosque)). Expect a brief bag check and a 10- to 25-minute queue at peak midday slots between April and October.
What scarves and clothing are provided vs better brought yourself?

Free headscarves, wrap-around skirts, and disposable shoe bags are lent at the visitor desk, but bringing your own lightweight scarf, slip-on shoes, and knee-covering clothes is cleaner, cooler, and faster. Borrowed synthetic wraps are hot in summer and add an extra stop at the loan counter before you enter the prayer hall.

Both men and women must cover shoulders and knees; tank tops, sleeveless dresses, and shorts above the knee are turned back until covered. Women must also cover their hair with a loose scarf. You will remove your shoes at the carpeted threshold and carry them inside in a provided bag, so wear clean socks and shoes without complicated laces.
How do you combine Blue Mosque, Hippodrome and Hagia Sophia?

Start at the Blue Mosque at 08:30, stroll across the Hippodrome monuments in 20 minutes, and cross Sultanahmet Park to Hagia Sophia's dedicated tourist entrance before noon prayer. Grouping these three stops on foot takes under three hours and eliminates back-and-forth walking.

Unlike the free Blue Mosque, [Hagia Sophia's upper gallery](https://muze.gen.tr/muze-detay/ayasofya) operates a separate ticketed tourist route priced at €25 for foreign visitors in 2026 (MuseumPass Istanbul is not valid; children under 8 enter free, per [Hagia Sophia Visitor Info](https://www.hagiasophia.com/hagia-sophia-tickets)). Between the two mosques, pause at the Obelisk of Theodosius, the Serpent Column, and the German Fountain along the former Byzantine chariot track of the Hippodrome.

Enter via the southwest Visitor Entrance on the Hippodrome (At Meydanı) side.
Wear slip-on shoes, clean socks, and clothing covering shoulders and knees.
Pack your own breathable headscarf rather than queuing for loaner wraps.
Silence your phone and turn off camera flash before stepping onto the prayer carpet.

faq.q: Do I need to book a Blue Mosque ticket online in 2026?
faq.a: No. Admission is completely free and no timed ticket exists. Guided tours are optional and do not bypass the security check or prayer-time closures.

faq.q: Can non-Muslims visit the Blue Mosque?
faq.a: Yes. Non-Muslim visitors are warmly welcomed outside the five daily prayer windows and Friday morning services, provided they follow the dress code and keep voices low.

faq.q: How long should I budget inside the Blue Mosque?
faq.a: Plan 30 to 45 minutes for the courtyard and interior hall, plus 15 to 25 minutes for security and entry queues during busy months.

faq.q: Is the Blue Mosque open on Fridays?
faq.a: Yes, but only in the afternoon. It remains closed to tourists all Friday morning for the weekly Jumu'ah prayer and typically reopens around 14:30.

faq.q: Are photography and video allowed inside?
faq.a: Yes, personal non-flash photography is allowed inside the visitor area. Avoid photographing worshippers directly and keep tripods packed away.

faq.q: Is the Blue Mosque wheelchair accessible?
faq.a: Yes. The courtyard and main visitor hall have ramped access from the visitor gate side, though the surrounding Sultanahmet cobblestones can be uneven.
